THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Heard learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
2.

The present appeal is directed against the judgment and award dated 17th September, 2016 passed in MVC No.877 of 2016 by the X Additional Judge Small Causes and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (for short hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal').

sentences.text: The appellant/petitioner has approached this Court in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. It is the case of the appellant/petitioner that on 3rd January, 2016 at 11.30 a.m. while he was proceeding on his motorcycle near Jain Temple, the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MP-9889 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the appellant/petitioner causing accident.

The appellant/petitioner contend that he sustained injuries and was immediately shifted NC: 2023:KHC:20822 to V.S. Acharya Hospital where he took the first aid and then he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bangalore and there he was an inpatient from 03rd to 13th January, 2016.

He was diagnosed to be having the injury of left ankle subluxation with medial malleoli, type B open fracture, closed fracture of proximal third of right humerus with radial nerve palsy, pubic rami fracture right side.
The appellant/petitioner contend that he underwent open reduction and internal fixation with DCP for right humerus and SSG of left ankle; and had spent Rs.5.00 lakh for treatment.

It was contended that the appellant/petitioner was working in Maruti Medical Centre, Banashankari III Stage, Bengaluru and was drawing a salary of Rs.14,500/-
per month and due to accident, he has lost the said job.

sentences.text:
It is further contended that the driver of the car was prosecuted by the police for rash and negligent driving and therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation from the owner and Insurer of the car who are arrayed as respondents 1 and 2.
4.

On being issued with notice by the Tribunal, respondents 1 and 2 appeared before the Tribunal and filed objections denying that the accident had occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the car.

Respondent NC: 2023:KHC:20822 No.1 contended that the negligence is on the part of the appellant/petitioner himself and that the respondent No.2- Inurance Company had issued the Policy of Insurance and as on the date of the accident, the Policy was in force and as such,
liability has to be fastened upon the respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
The respondent No.2 contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, imaginary and untenable.

sentences.text: On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues and the appellant/petitioner was examined as PW1 and marked exhibits P1 to P19 were marked.
The Doctor of Hosmat Hospital was examined as PW2.
No evidence was led on behalf of respondents.

After hearing both the sides,
the Tribunal, by impugned judgment, award compensation of Rs.5,87,548/-.
Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before the Court in this appeal.
6. On issuance of notice, the respondent-Insurance Company has appeared through its Counsel and notice to NC: 2023:KHC:20822 respondent No.1 was dispensed with.
The records of Tribunal have been secured.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that even though PW2 has stated that disability was to the extent of 35% to the whole body, the Tribunal has assessed it at 22%, which is not proper and correct.
Further, he submits that the notional income of the petitioner was also not properly considered by the Tribunal and the future medical expenses, as deposed by PW2, was not considered by the Tribunal.
Therefore, he contends that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is erroneous and there is a need for enhancement.

8. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the Respondent No.2-Insurance Company has defended the award passed by the Tribunal contending that the quantum of compensation awarded under various heads are proper, sufficient and just.

9. The Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.7,000/- per month and holding that the petitioner had suffered disability of 22%, came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled for compensation as NC: 2023:KHC:20822 stated above.

The Tribunal has awarded the compensation under different heads as below:

sentences.text: A perusal of evidence of PW2 discloses that he has assessed the disability to the upper limb at 45% and disability to the lower limp at 65%.
PW2, in his affidavit, has elaborately stated the reasons for coming to such conclusion.
It is evident that PW2 has assessed the physical disability of the petitioner but no where in the affidavit of PW2 there is any mention about the avocation of the petitioner.
Therefore, disability assessed by PW2 is physical disability and the Tribunal should have considered the functional disability of the petitioner.
A perusal of the impugned judgment and award do not show any reasoning as to how the physical disability of 31% has NC: 2023:KHC:20822 translated into functional disability of 22%.
It is relevant to note that the appellant/petitioner claims that he was working in a Medical Shop and was earning Rs.14,500/- per month.

There is absolutely no documentary evidence placed on record by the appellant/petitioner to establish this aspect and hence the Tribunal was justified in considering the notional income instead of the income of Rs.14,500/-, as contended by the appellant/petitioner.
Even though the contention of the petitioner that he was earning Rs.14,500/- per month cannot be considered, the fact that he was working in a medical shop cannot be disputed.
Obviously, the appellant/petitioner was aged about 20 years as on the date of accident and therefore, it can be said that he was working and earning a small livelihood.
The disability on account of injuries sustained by him, when juxtaposed with the avocation of the petitioner, would not cause much inconvenience.
It is pertinent to note that the fusion of the ankle joint is one of the aspect which he has to bear for the rest of the life.
It would be difficult to accept that it may improve.

Considering this aspect as well as the age of the petitioner and that his movements would be restricted in the rest of his life which would eventually curtail NC:
2023:KHC:20822 the better opportunities in his life, it would be just and proper to hold the functional disability at 25%.
11.
The notional income considered by the Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- per month appears to be without any basis.
The guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority indicate that for the accident of the year 2016, the notional income of Rs.9,500/- per month is prescribed.

In umpteen number of decisions, this Court has held that the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, the notional income of the appellant/petitioner is taken at Rs.9,500/- per month.

In view of the above conclusion in respect of the notional income, as well as the disability, the loss of future income, keeping in view the disability, is calculated as Rs.5,13,000/- (Rs.9,500/- x 12 x 18 x 25%).

As a consequence, the loss of income during the laid up period is also required to be considered,
accordingly it comes to Rs.38,000/- (Rs.9,500/- x 4).
12. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head 'pain and suffering'.

In view of three major NC: 2023:KHC:20822 fractures being suffered by the appellant/petitioner, it would be appropriate to award sum of Rs.60,000/- under the head 'pain and suffering'.
13.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,19,908/- and Rs.12,000/- under the head medical expenses and attendant charges respectively and the same do not require any enhancement.
14. PW2 has stated that the petitioner would be requiring a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- as future medical expenses, since there is a need for de-fusion of the ankle joint.
It is pertinent to note that the assessment of such future requirement is not placed on record.

It is only in the affidavit of PW2 that B K Jeevan vs General Manager on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57657531/
4 he has assessed the disability.
